setup.start: npm install; npm run local:start; open http://localhost:5173/
setup.database: Keep the existing MONGODB_URI. Local MongoDB is configured; use an Atlas URI only when you have that deployment. No migration or seeding is needed.
setup.publicOrigin: Use HTTPS and set APP_ORIGIN to the actual origin for access from other devices. Localhost is not a public URL.
setup.execution: Set JUDGE0_URL and provider-required JUDGE0_API_KEY, JUDGE0_AUTH_HEADER, JUDGE0_RAPIDAPI_HOST. Run npm run code:check. See docs/CODE-EXECUTION.md. Submitted programs are never executed on the app server.
setup.relay: Set STUN_URL and reachable TURN_URL (UDP/TCP/TLS as appropriate), TURN_SECRET and TURN_TTL_SECONDS. Test real media between separate networks; see deploy/.
setup.dependencies: pdfjs-dist is a direct dependency with a locally bundled worker; jsdom and its types are development-only.

remainingVerification: Two real authenticated sessions/devices: both cameras and audio, readable candidate screen beside camera, device toggles, denial/unplug/recovery, stop-sharing, network loss/reconnect and track cleanup on end.
Visual and keyboard/screen-reader checks of setup, waiting, all internal panels and modals in both themes on desktop, tablet and mobile.
Configure/test a live Judge0 runner: Java success, compilation/runtime failures, timeout and exact-version output visible to HR.
Deploy HTTPS and TURN and test a real cross-network call. No hosting or relay account was created.
Optional face analysis requires separate consent controls and real-camera validation before being connected to the new room.
limits: Peer-to-peer signaling restricts the dedicated screen slot; it cannot attest that a modified client's allowed webcam track originated from a camera. An SFU would be needed for media-server publication control.
Camera readiness, display surface and activity are browser-reported, not tamper-proof. External application identity and OS switching cannot be controlled.
Tab backup/retry supports transient disconnect, but browser storage deletion or closing before delivery can lose unsent data. Execution is not simulated offline.
No zero-error or production-readiness claim is made.
